examples.text: Er is hars uit dat stuk hout gedruppeld.
Na die oogoperatie heb ik nog enige tijd gedruppeld, maar het was snel weer geheeld.
Anna druppelde regelmatig vocht op de lamsbout.
Pass auf, dass du mit dem nassen Handtuch nicht tropfst.
Der Wasserhahn tropfte die ganze Nacht.
„Sie brachte ihm auch frische Wäsche, tropfte Arznei auf Löffel, half ihm beim Frischmachen.“
„Ein Wasserhahn tropft. Leilani stellt einen Messbecher unter den Wasserhahn und stellt fest, dass in 20 Minuten 16ml Wasser in den Messbecher tropfen.“
„Von der Kelter tropft dann zuckersüßer Saft.“

glosses: To fall one drop at a time.

examples.text: Listening to the tap next door drip all night drove me mad!
Does the sink drip, or have I just spilt water over the floor?
After putting oil on the side of the salad, the chef should drip a little vinegar in the oil.
My broken pen dripped ink onto the table.

c. 1726, Alexander Pope (probable author), The Lamentation of Glumdalclitch
Which from the thatch drips fast a shower of rain.

Philander went into the next room[…]and came back with a salt mackerel that dripped brine like a rainstorm. Then he put the coffee pot on the stove and rummaged out a loaf of dry bread and some hardtack.
The Old Hall simply drips with masterpieces of the Flemish painters.
The duchess was dripping with jewels.
The weather isn't so bad. I mean, it's dripping, but you're not going to get so wet.

glosses: To be wet, to be soaked.
To whine or complain consistently; to grumble.

examples.text: The Women's Royal Naval Service was integrated with the Royal Navy in November 1993. […] Men interviewed by Public Eye (April, 1994) said they should 'stop dripping about it' and that women should learn to 'take it like a man […]

The government had been slowly running down the Royal Navy Organisation to save money on various peoples' budgets, so now we had to sub-contract ships to go to war! So stop dripping and "make it so", all those admirals can't be wrong!
I'm sorry for drippin', but drip is what I do. And one of these days, I'm gon' get dressed and drip all over you.
I put a drip of vanilla extract in my hot cocoa.
I need a bucket to catch the drips.

glosses: A falling or letting fall in drops; act of dripping.

examples.text: the light drip of the suspended oar

glosses: An apparatus that slowly releases a liquid, especially one that intravenously releases drugs into a patient's bloodstream.

examples.text: He's not doing so well. The doctors have put him on a drip.

glosses: A limp, ineffectual, or uninteresting person.

examples.text: He couldn't even summon up the courage to ask her name... what a drip!

Because most of the blokes I fancy think l'm stupid and pointless—and, so, they just bonk me and then leave me. And the kind of blokes that do fancy me, I think are drips. I can't even be bothered to bonk them. Which does sort of leave me a bit nowhere.

glosses: That part of a cornice, sill course, or other horizontal member, which projects beyond the rest, and has a section designed to throw off rainwater.
Style; swagger; fashionable and/or expensive clothing.

examples.text: His drip is looking fine, especially the Supreme t-shirt.
Hailey decided to show off her drip with a soft, white fluff jacket […]
The cold weather can't stop your drip.
Staying true to their purpose, all this exciting drip will be available at the most pocket-friendly prices.

glosses: Alternative letter-case form of DRIP (“dividend reinvestment plan”)

examples.text: Cependant Pierrat Torterue faisait dégoutter sur le pavé les lanières rouges et gorgées de sang.

Par moments, quand ce ruissellement s’arrête, là-bas, au fond, ce sont des gouttes qui tombent une à une, comme après un dégel ou une grande pluie. On dirait que le brouillard, amassé sur les toits, sur les murs, se fond à la chaleur du poêle et dégoutte continuellement.
La sueur et le sang dégouttaient de ses cheveux et coulaient confondus sur son visage.
Les gouttes de pluie dégouttaient d’en haut, faisant une sorte de rideau à la paille humide.

glosses: Faire tomber goutte à goutte de l’eau, de la sueur, etc.

examples.text: Et alors, […], j'aperçus Kostaki, pâle comme je l'avais vu sur la litière; ses longs cheveux noirs, épars sur ses épaules, dégouttaient de sang.
Ses jambes tremblaient, et en passant la main sur son visage, il s’aperçut qu’il dégouttait de sueur.
Il pleuvait il n’y a qu’un moment, les toits dégouttent encore.
Ses cheveux dégouttent.

glosses: Dicho de un líquido: Salir o fluir en pequeñas porciones (gota a gota).
Dicho de una cosa: Echar gotas de líquido o dejarlas caer.
Caer gotas pequeñas, especialmente cuando va a comenzar a llover.
